name: Suvomipic

lead: Suvomipic (PP405) is an experimental scalp gel from Pelage Pharmaceuticals aimed at androgenetic hair loss. People following hair loss research watch it as a possible new regrowth option.

It inhibits the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier, which is thought to push dormant follicle stem cells toward glycolysis and growth. In preliminary phase 2a results released in June 2025, 31% of men reached a hair density gain of 20% or more at eight weeks, with no placebo responders; the trial was designed mainly to assess safety.

paras: It is a once-daily topical used in clinical trials only. It is not available outside studies, and phase 3 trials were planned for 2026.
It is investigational and not approved anywhere. Safety data are early-phase and the results come from the company.

studies.title: Development of Novel Mitochondrial Pyruvate Carrier Inhibitors to Treat Hair Loss.

chain: Follicle stem cells switch to growth
angle.text: Suvomipic is an experimental once-daily scalp gel that blocks the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier, which is thought to switch follicle stem cells toward growth and regrow scalp hair. Company-reported phase 2a results showed density gains at eight weeks.

lead: Suvomipic (developmental code PP405) is an experimental topical drug for hair loss developed by Pelage Pharmaceuticals, a company spun out of UCLA in 2018.[1] It is described as a possible first-in-class compound that inhibits the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier (MPC1 and MPC2), which is thought to raise pyruvate and push hair follicle stem cells toward glycolysis and growth.[1]

It is formulated as a 0.05% scalp gel applied once daily.[1] In preliminary phase 2a results released in June 2025, 31% of men with advanced baldness had a hair density increase of 20% or more at eight weeks, versus none of the placebo group; the trial was designed mainly to assess safety.[1] It is not approved anywhere.

paras: First human trials began in 2023 in Orange County, California; phase 1 and phase 2a have been completed.[1] The June 2025 phase 2a report described above came from a preliminary analysis and a three-month open-label extension was completed, with data promised for 2026 and phase 3 planned for 2026.[1] Earliest possible approval is estimated by Wikipedia at 2027 to 2029.[1] Peer-reviewed full results were not located in the sources reviewed.
Wikipedia notes that Pelage has said suvomipic is not JXL069, while a WHO international nonproprietary name list identifies it as JXL069, an unresolved discrepancy.[1]

timeline.event: Pelage Pharmaceuticals founded as a UCLA spin-out.[1]
